claims.statement: The document-expansion method docT5query generalizes well, slightly outperforming BM25 on average (+1.6%) and beating it on 11 of 18 datasets.

Dense bi-encoder retrievers underperform BM25 on average zero-shot performance (DPR -47.7%, ANCE -7.4%, TAS-B -2.8%); DPR, the only evaluated system not trained on MS MARCO, generalizes worst overall and dense retrievers underperform particularly under large domain or task shift.
Among dense retrievers, TAS-B gives the best zero-shot generalization, outperforming ANCE on 14 of 18 datasets and DPR on 17 of 18 datasets.

The authors speculate that TAS-B's stronger generalization stems from its training setup (in-batch negatives combined with a Margin-MSE loss, under knowledge distillation from a strong teacher ensemble), rather than from architecture alone.

limitations.statement: All 18 BEIR datasets are English-only; multilingual and cross-lingual retrieval are untested.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Generalization findings are bounded to English text; they say nothing about cross-lingual or multilingual zero-shot retrieval.

limitations.statement: Because transformer-based approaches truncate at 512 word pieces, documents are effectively limited to at most a few hundred words in these experiments; long-document retrieval is untested.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The architecture ranking (e.g. re-ranking/late-interaction generalizing best) is not established for long-document collections, where the same truncation would discard most of the document.

limitations.statement: Only pure textual query-document matching is evaluated; no auxiliary ranking signals such as PageRank, recency, authority score, or click-through rate are incorporated.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Findings describe text-matching capability only; real deployed systems that combine text relevance with such signals may behave differently.

limitations.statement: Evaluation covers only one or two document fields (e.g. title and passage); true multi-field retrieval (e.g. title, abstract, body, authors, venue for scientific documents) is not tested.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Results may not extend to retrieval settings where combining evidence across several fields matters.

limitations.statement: The benchmark and its comparisons target systems built to generalize broadly across tasks; a specialized, task-specific model could still outperform the generalist systems compared here on an individual task.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The architecture ranking is a ranking of zero-shot generalization capability, not proof that no better task-specific alternative exists for any single dataset.

limitations.statement: No error bars or seed/replicate variance are reported for any of the zero-shot comparisons, because most evaluated systems are third-party pre-trained checkpoints without accessible re-training code, making re-training infeasible in many cases.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Close rankings (e.g. TAS-B vs. ColBERT vs. docT5query, within a few points of each other on average) should be read as point estimates from a single run, not as statistically distinguished.

limitations.statement: Total compute used is not fully reported; only hardware types (GPU/CPU models) are given for the efficiency measurements.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Absolute efficiency numbers are tied to the specific hardware described and cannot be converted to a total-compute or cost figure from the source alone.

limitations.statement: The annotation-pooling-bias measurement (Hole@10 and manual re-annotation) was carried out on one dataset, TREC-COVID; the paper argues by analogy (citing similar lexical-matching-based candidate selection for BioASQ and Signal-1M) that comparable bias likely affects other BEIR datasets, but does not measure its size there.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The specific magnitude of annotation bias (Hole@10 percentages, score changes) is established only for TREC-COVID; its presence elsewhere in BEIR is a documented but untested inference.
